math_plain: Combines a structured community-detection model with sparse attention scoring to predict missing links in networks by learning which pairs of nodes should be connected.
why_math: It works because community structure genuinely explains network connectivity: nodes in the same group connect more often, so learning this structure lets you predict unobserved links. The attention mechanism captures which long-range patterns matter without checking every possible pair.

why_math: It works because randomized comment variants isolate what caused the sharing decision. Comparing outcomes when only the comment changes reveals which factors actually drive behavior versus what merely appears correlated.

math_plain: Decomposes event streams with mixed categorical and numeric attributes into latent components tracking group structure and temporal trends to flag unusual group-level patterns.
why_math: It works because real event data clusters naturally: similar events come from the same underlying group activity. Modeling each attribute type's true statistical shape lets you detect when a group's behavior shifts or becomes unusual, rather than losing signal by forcing all attributes into one shape.

math_plain: Clusters phishing URLs by similarity, ranks their dissemination leverage across decentralized gateways, and estimates impact of blocking small dominant clusters.
why_math: It works because real-world attacks concentrate: blocking the few most-used dissemination channels removes availability for most phishing content. Clustering by behavior finds which attacks are coordinated variants of the same campaign, so you target root causes instead of chasing copies.

math_plain: Identifies which training examples cause bias in recommendations, then removes their influence on the model to improve fairness without full retraining.
why_math: It works because removing the true bias-causing examples fixes the model at its core. You don't need to retrain from scratch; small adjustments that undo the influence of those few examples efficiently flip wrong predictions back to fair ones.

why_math: It works because humans recognize emotion partly through specific word choices and grammar patterns that reliably appear together. Adding these explicit signals lets the model see what matters faster and stays robust when the neural patterns encounter new data.

math_plain: Simulates diverse unusual graph variants using learned prompts and filters graph substructures to keep only those that distinguish normal from anomalous graphs.
why_math: It works because rare anomalies are too scarce to learn from alone; generating synthetic variants broadens your view of what abnormal looks like. Filtering substructures keeps the signal for abnormality while noise-substructures from normal graphs stop misleading you.

math_plain: Diagnoses rewriting problems in search queries, then learns human-like fixes through supervised training and preference-aligned beam search ranking.
why_math: It works because humans rewrite queries systematically: certain problems map to certain fixes. Learning this mapping directly from human examples, then using ranked search to pick rewrites that match both human and retrieval-system preferences, produces more natural and effective query corrections.

math_plain: Groups table instances into clusters, generates synthetic query examples for partial tables across clusters, and fine-tunes embedding models using hard-negative contrastive pairs.
why_math: It works because diverse training examples teach the model to handle semantic variation. Grouping tables ensures you see the full semantic range. Hard-negative pairs force the model to push apart genuinely different cases, so it learns precise, robust distance metrics for table-query matching.

math_plain: Extracts visual patterns from satellite imagery and combines them with spatial and temporal patterns to jointly score traffic predictions node by node.
why_math: It works because real traffic depends on overlapping factors: road layout, weather, events, congestion. Treating each modality separately loses their interactions; combining visual context with spatial neighbors and time history captures the full cause, so predictions account for all factors simultaneously.

math_plain: Converts graph anomaly detection into a tabular problem by enriching node features with structural summaries, then applies pre-trained tabular models for cross-domain generalization.
why_math: It works because tabular models already solve the hard parts: handling diverse feature types and generalizing to new domains via synthetic pre-training. Structure itself is just another feature; once you express it as numbers alongside node attributes, tabular models see it naturally and transfer across graphs.

math_plain: Learns multi-scale features of human behavior, objects, and background context from video, then adaptively weights them to predict threat location and explain threat causes.
why_math: It works because threats arise from interactions of multiple elements: a person's action, an object involved, and the setting all matter.
